title: 10 - DOR Registry
description:
**Purpose:** operational view of the Drone Operator Registry — operator onboarding, verification backlog, fleet inventory and registration validity.

**Data source:** `dor-be-mysql` — the LIVE `dor_be` MariaDB schema on `core-database`, via a SELECT-only, column-scoped `grafana_ro` account.

**Privacy:** no personal data is queried or displayed. Names, emails, phones, birthdates, addresses and document identifiers are not granted to the Grafana account.

**Interpretation:** the registration funnel is cumulative — each stage is a strict subset of the previous one, so a narrowing funnel is normal and the gaps are backlog.

**Performance:** this queries a live transactional database serving the /pm/ portal. All panels aggregate; refresh is 5m by design. Do not lower it.

panels.title: Operators
panels.description: Rows in `organisations`. An operator is an organisation in the registry.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations

panels.title: Verified Operators
panels.description: organisations.verified = 1.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE verified = 1

panels.title: Active Operators
panels.description: organisations.active = 1.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE active = 1

panels.title: Registered Users
panels.description: Rows in `users` — individuals, not organisations.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM users

panels.title: Drones
panels.description: Rows in `drones` (the UAS subtype of `assets`).

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM drones

panels.title: Assets
panels.description: All fleet assets, drones included.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM assets

panels.title: Registration Funnel — Registered → Verified → Active
panels.description: Each stage is a strict subset of the one before: every organisation is Registered; Verified adds verified=1; Active adds active=1 on top of verified. A wide gap between stages is onboarding backlog, not an error.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT '1 Registered' AS stage, COUNT(*) AS operators FROM organisations
UNION ALL
SELECT '2 Verified',  COUNT(*) FROM organisations WHERE verified = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT '3 Active',    COUNT(*) FROM organisations WHERE verified = 1 AND active = 1
ORDER BY stage

panels.title: Operators by Status
panels.description: Cross-tab of organisations.verified and organisations.active. 'Awaiting Verification' is the actionable bucket — active but not yet verified.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN verified = 1 AND active = 1 THEN 'Verified & Active'
    WHEN verified = 1 AND active = 0 THEN 'Verified, Inactive'
    WHEN verified = 0 AND active = 1 THEN 'Awaiting Verification'
    ELSE 'Unverified & Inactive'
  END AS status,
  COUNT(*) AS operators
FROM organisations
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY operators DESC

panels.title: Operators Awaiting Verification
panels.description: organisations.verified = 0. These cannot complete onboarding.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE verified = 0

panels.title: Users Awaiting Verification
panels.description: users.verified = 0.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM users WHERE verified = 0

panels.title: Oldest Unverified Operator
panels.description: Age of the longest-waiting unverified organisation. The number that matters for onboarding SLA — a small backlog that is very old is still a problem.

targets.rawSql: SELECT IFNULL(MAX(DATEDIFF(NOW(), created_at)), 0) AS value FROM organisations WHERE verified = 0

panels.title: Unverified Operators
panels.description: Organisations with verified = 0, oldest first. `name` is a company name, not personal data. No contact details are queried — the Grafana account has no grant on phone, VAT or address columns.

targets.rawSql: SELECT name AS Operator, created_at AS Registered, DATEDIFF(NOW(), created_at) AS `Days Waiting`, IF(active = 1, 'active', 'inactive') AS Status FROM organisations WHERE verified = 0 ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Drones per Operator
panels.description: LEFT JOIN so operators with no fleet still appear as 0 — a registered operator with zero drones is meaningful, and an inner join would hide it. `drones` is the UAS subtype of `assets`, keyed on the same asset_id.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT o.name AS Operator,
       COUNT(DISTINCT d.asset_id) AS Drones,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.asset_id) AS `Total Assets`
FROM organisations o
LEFT JOIN assets a ON a.org_id = o.org_id
LEFT JOIN drones d ON d.asset_id = a.asset_id
GROUP BY o.org_id, o.name
ORDER BY Drones DESC, `Total Assets` DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Drones by UAS Class
panels.description: drones.uas_class — the EU open-category class marking (C0–C4).

targets.rawSql: SELECT IFNULL(NULLIF(uas_class, ''), 'unspecified') AS uas_class, COUNT(*) AS drones FROM drones GROUP BY uas_class ORDER BY drones DESC

panels.title: Assets by Type
panels.description: assets.type across the whole registry.

targets.rawSql: SELECT IFNULL(NULLIF(type, ''), 'unspecified') AS type, COUNT(*) AS assets FROM assets GROUP BY type ORDER BY assets DESC

panels.title: Asset Registrations Over Time
panels.description: assets.created_at, bucketed daily. Shows fleet growth.

targets.rawSql: SELECT DATE(created_at) AS time, COUNT(*) AS 'assets registered' FROM assets GROUP BY DATE(created_at) ORDER BY time

panels.title: Operator Registrations Over Time
panels.description: organisations.created_at, bucketed daily.

targets.rawSql: SELECT DATE(created_at) AS time, COUNT(*) AS 'operators registered' FROM organisations GROUP BY DATE(created_at) ORDER BY time

panels.title: Org Registration Documents
panels.description: Rows in organisation_registration_documents.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisation_registration_documents

panels.title: User Verification Documents
panels.description: Rows in user_verification_documents.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM user_verification_documents

panels.title: Operators With No Registration Document
panels.description: Organisations that have never uploaded a registration document — usually the reason an operator is stuck unverified.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM organisation_registration_documents d WHERE d.org_id = o.org_id)

panels.title: Document Activity by Operator
panels.description: Per-organisation document counts and most recent upload. File names and document UUIDs are deliberately NOT queried — the Grafana account has no grant on those columns.

targets.rawSql: SELECT o.name AS Operator, COUNT(d.ovd_id) AS Documents, MAX(d.updated_at) AS `Last Upload` FROM organisations o LEFT JOIN organisation_registration_documents d ON d.org_id = o.org_id GROUP BY o.org_id, o.name ORDER BY Documents DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Expired Registrations
panels.description: organisations.reg_no_expires_at in the past. These operators are no longer validly registered.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE reg_no_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND reg_no_expires_at < CURDATE()

panels.title: Expiring Within 30 Days
panels.description: Registrations lapsing soon — the actionable renewal queue.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE reg_no_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND reg_no_expires_at BETWEEN CURDATE() AND DATE_ADD(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)

panels.title: No Registration Number
panels.description: organisations.registration_no is NULL or empty.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE registration_no IS NULL OR registration_no = ''

panels.title: Legal Entities
panels.description: organisations.legal_entity = 1 (company rather than individual operator).

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM organisations WHERE legal_entity = 1

panels.title: Identity Sync Health — Keycloak vs DOR database
Keycloak Identities (utm-dor)
panels.description: Users in the Keycloak utm-dor realm. Counts identities only — no credentials, attributes or sessions are readable by this account.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM dor_keycloak.user_entity ue JOIN dor_keycloak.realm r ON r.id = ue.realm_id WHERE r.name = 'utm-dor'

panels.title: DOR Database Users
panels.description: Rows in dor_be.users.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM dor_be.users

panels.title: Sync Divergence
panels.description: Absolute difference between the two. SHOULD BE 0. Any non-zero value means an account exists on one side only — the signature of a half-completed registration.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ABS( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dor_keycloak.user_entity ue JOIN dor_keycloak.realm r ON r.id = ue.realm_id WHERE r.name = 'utm-dor') - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dor_be.users) ) AS value

options.content:
**Divergence should be 0.**

`com.skyzr.keycloak` (in `basic-storage-provider-1.0.jar`) is compiled against `javax.ws.rs` but runs on **Keycloak 25**, which uses `jakarta.ws.rs`. REGISTER events therefore fail with `NoClassDefFoundError: javax/ws/rs/core/Response$Status` **after** the Keycloak identity is created but **before** DOR provisioning finishes.

Result: an identity exists in Keycloak with no usable DOR account — the user can authenticate but every admin action on them returns 500 (`User could not be found in Keycloak`, or the reverse).

This panel makes an otherwise silent defect visible. It is a **detector, not a fix** — the JAR must be rebuilt against Jakarta.

panels.title: Scope, data protection and current volume

options.content:
### What this dashboard reads

Elasticsearch-backed dashboards in this suite read historical statistics copies. **This one queries `dor_be` directly** — the live MariaDB behind the `/pm/` portal. Figures are current, not a snapshot.

Because it is a live transactional database, every panel aggregates and the dashboard refreshes at **5m**, not the 30s used for infrastructure dashboards.

### Data protection

Grafana connects as `grafana_ro`, which holds **SELECT-only, column-scoped** grants on `dor_be`. Not granted, and therefore unreachable even from Explore:

- `users.email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone`, `birthdate`
- `users.internal_notes`, `activity_log`, `pilot_number`, `skid`
- `organisations.phone`, `vat_no`, `org_id_no`, `insurance_no`, `internal_notes`
- document `file_name` and `*_uuid` columns
- the entire `addresses` table

Organisation **names** are shown — those are company identifiers, not personal data.
